lead: At microwave frequencies you cannot clip a multimeter across a wave. Wavelengths are millimetres, so voltage and current vary along the line. Engineers measure indirect quantities: standing-wave ratio from a slotted line, power with thermal sensors, frequency with a cavity wavemeter, and S-parameters with a vector network analyser. These measurements check filters, couplers, amplifiers and antennas before a system is deployed. A wrong calibration can make a bad component look good. VSWR, power, frequency and S-parameters are the basic bench checks in any microwave lab.
prereq: You need Unit 1 on standing waves, reflection coefficient and VSWR, and 4.1 S-parameters and the scattering matrix.

sections.h3: VSWR and guide wavelength from a slotted line

blocks.text: A slotted line is a section of coaxial line or waveguide with a narrow longitudinal slot. A small probe enters the slot and samples the electric field at one point. You move the probe along the line and watch a detector. The probe draws very little power; it only samples the field.

When the load is not matched, incident and reflected waves add and subtract. The envelope has maxima and minima. Define V<sub>max</sub> as the maximum probe voltage and V<sub>min</sub> as the minimum probe voltage, both in volts.

blocks.where: |Γ| is the magnitude of the load reflection coefficient, a number from 0 to 1; V<sub>max</sub> and V<sub>min</sub> are the maximum and minimum RF voltages along the line, in volts.
VSWR is the voltage standing-wave ratio, a number ≥ 1; it has no unit.

blocks.text: A square-law detector gives a DC output proportional to RF power, so meter reading M follows M ∝ V². If the meter is calibrated in power, take square roots before using the voltage formulas: VSWR = √(M<sub>max</sub> / M<sub>min</sub>). If the meter is calibrated in voltage, use the readings directly.
The guide wavelength λ<sub>g</sub> is twice the distance between adjacent minima. Successive minima are half a guide wavelength apart, not one full guide wavelength.

blocks.where: λ<sub>g</sub> is the guide wavelength in metres; d is the distance between two adjacent minima in metres.

items: Connect the source, slotted line and unknown load; keep the source level fixed.
Move the probe and record V<sub>max</sub> and V<sub>min</sub>.
Compute |Γ| and VSWR from the two voltages.
Measure d between two adjacent minima.

blocks.text: Power is the basic microwave quantity. A power sensor absorbs the RF signal and converts it to heat or to a DC voltage. Three common sensors are bolometer, thermistor and thermocouple.

items: Bolometer: a temperature-sensitive resistor in a bridge. RF power heats it; the bridge restores balance. The DC substitute power equals the RF power.
Thermistor: a semiconductor bead whose resistance falls with temperature. It uses the same DC-substitution idea.
Thermocouple: RF heats a hot junction; a DC voltage appears at the cold junction, proportional to absorbed power.
Directional coupler: samples a known small fraction of the main-line power. A 20 dB coupler gives one hundredth of the main power at the coupled port.

blocks.text: A cavity wavemeter measures frequency. It is a tunable high-Q cavity coupled to the line. Tune the cavity until it absorbs power and the meter dips; the calibrated dial then reads frequency. For lower microwave bands, an electronic counter counts cycles directly, and a prescaler extends its range.

sections.h3: Vector network analyser and SOLT calibration

blocks.text: A vector network analyser sends a known incident wave into a port and measures the reflected and transmitted waves. It reports complex S-parameters: magnitude and phase. For a two-port, S11 is input reflection, S21 is forward transmission, S12 is reverse transmission, and S22 is output reflection. This is the practical measurement of the matrix in 4.1.

Raw VNA data has systematic errors: directivity, source match, load match and frequency tracking. Calibration measures known standards at the reference plane and computes correction. SOLT uses Short, Open, Load and Thru. Short gives Γ = −1; Open gives Γ = +1; Load gives Γ = 0; Thru connects the two ports.

After calibration, the VNA applies error correction to every sweep. Save the calibration and check it with a known air line or attenuator. Uncalibrated data is not final; a poor calibration can hide a bad connector.

blocks.where: |S<sub>21</sub>| is the forward voltage gain magnitude, a ratio; S<sub>21,dB</sub> is the same gain in decibels.

figure.caption: The probe samples the standing wave along the slotted line. The meter gives Vmax = 5 V and Vmin = 1 V; the detector is square law, so work in voltage or take square roots of power readings.

spec.title: Slotted-line VSWR measurement
spec.aria: A 10 GHz source feeds a slotted line whose standing-wave minima are 15 mm apart; a moving probe samples the field, a square-law detector converts it, and a meter reads Vmax 5 V and Vmin 1 V.

examples.question: A slotted-line measurement at 10 GHz gives a maximum probe voltage of 5 V and a minimum of 1 V. The probe is calibrated in volts. The distance between successive minima is 15 mm. Calculate VSWR, the magnitude of the reflection coefficient, and the guide wavelength.
steps: Distance between adjacent minima d = 15 mm = 0.015 m.
examples.check:
Vmax = 5.0
Vmin = 1.0
d_mm = 15.0
vswr = Vmax / Vmin
gamma = abs((Vmax - Vmin) / (Vmax + Vmin))
lambda_g_mm = 2.0 * d_mm
print(f"{vswr:.1f}")
print(f"{gamma:.3f}")
print(f"{lambda_g_mm:.1f}")

code.code:
Vmax = 5.0
Vmin = 1.0
d_mm = 15.0
print(f"{Vmax / Vmin:.1f}")
print(f"{(Vmax - Vmin) / (Vmax + Vmin):.3f}")
print(f"{2.0 * d_mm:.1f}")

traps: Using the distance between adjacent minima as λg. Adjacent minima are half a guide wavelength apart, so λg = 2d.
Forgetting that a square-law detector reads power. The meter reading follows V², so take square roots before using Vmax / Vmin.
Writing VSWR as (Vmax + Vmin) / (Vmax − Vmin). The correct ratio is Vmax / Vmin, always ≥ 1.
Treating uncalibrated VNA data as final. SOLT calibration and error correction must be applied at the reference plane.
Confusing a cavity wavemeter with a power meter. The wavemeter is tuned until it absorbs power; the dip gives frequency, not power.

quiz.q: Define VSWR and give its formula in terms of Vmax and Vmin.
quiz.a: VSWR is the ratio of maximum to minimum voltage on a standing-wave pattern: VSWR = Vmax / Vmin. It is a number ≥ 1 and has no unit.

quiz.q: Name three types of microwave power sensors.
Why must a square-law detector reading be square-rooted before calculating VSWR from voltages?
quiz.a: A square-law detector output is proportional to RF power, and power is proportional to voltage squared. The VSWR formula uses voltage amplitudes, so the square root converts the power readings back to voltage ratios.

quiz.q: What does SOLT stand for in VNA calibration, and what does each standard do?
quiz.a: SOLT means Short, Open, Load, Thru. Short gives Γ = −1; Open gives Γ = +1; Load gives Γ = 0; Thru connects the two ports for transmission calibration. These known standards let the VNA remove systematic errors.

quiz.q: A square-law detector reads 9 mW at a maximum and 1 mW at a minimum. Find the VSWR.
quiz.a: For a square-law detector, VSWR = √(Mmax / Mmin) = √(9 mW / 1 mW) = √9 = 3.0.

quiz.q: A 20 dB directional coupler samples 10 mW at its coupled port. Estimate the power in the main line.
quiz.a: A 20 dB coupler gives one hundredth of the main power at the coupled port. Main power = 10 mW × 100 = 1000 mW = 1.0 W.

quiz.q: An engineer measures the distance between adjacent minima as 20 mm and calls it λg. What is the correct guide wavelength and the error?
quiz.a: Adjacent minima are half a guide wavelength apart, so λg = 2 × 20 mm = 40 mm. Calling 20 mm λg underestimates the guide wavelength by a factor of 2.

quiz.q: Why is an uncalibrated VNA sweep not acceptable for a final S11 measurement?
quiz.a: Raw VNA data contains systematic errors from directivity, source match, load match and tracking. Without SOLT calibration and error correction, a good match can look poor or a poor match can look good. Final S11 values must be corrected at the reference plane.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern labs use vector network analysers with electronic calibration modules, on-wafer probes for MMICs, and real-time error correction. Power metrology uses traceable calorimeters and microcalorimeters at national standards laboratories. Search terms: TRL calibration, electronic calibration module, on-wafer S-parameter measurement, microcalorimeter power standard.
